transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Nimbus Eng), Dasha Petrov (Nimbus PM), Liam O'Neill (Nimbus SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Goal: scope a 4-week POC to validate OpenAI-compatible endpoints with function/tool calling + structured JSON output for Nimbus's document ingestion and QA assistant workload.
- Key success criteria: matched quality to current embeddings/generation baseline, p95 latency < 450ms for standard queries, ability to sustain 120 concurrent requests with queuing < 2s, and validated structured output schema for compliance.
- Benchmarks: Redwood to run initial 2-hour load + comparison to current OpenAI+in-house routing.

Topics: success criteria; workload sizing; SDK vs direct OpenAI-compat endpoints; function calling & structured outputs; security/compliance artifacts; timeline and next steps.

Transcript: 
[00:00:03] Alex (Redwood AE): All right hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick intro from our side, I'm Alex, I'm the AE and Priya is our solutions engineer and we'll be driving the pilot set up.
[00:00:15] Priya (Redwood SE): Hi hi, good to meet you all. Quick check do we have everyone who will own sample data and SRE?
[00:00:22] Samir (Nimbus Eng): Yep that's me, Samir. Dasha on product and Liam's on SRE so we should be good.
[00:00:28] Dasha (Nimbus PM): Hey thanks for the intro. High level we want to replace part of our doc QA pipeline with an on-prem friendly flow, but we also want OpenAI-compat endpoints so our existing SDKs don't need much change.
[00:00:40] Liam (Nimbus SRE): And TOS note, we need a private deployment option eventually, but pilot can be hosted if the data samples are synthetic.

[00:01:05] Alex: Great, um let's start with success criteria, what would make this POC a win for you? Dasha?
[00:01:12] Dasha: Key things, one is accuracy parity — the new pipeline should match or exceed our current assistant's F1 on entity extraction tasks, second is latency we need p95 under about 450 to 500 ms for our default route, and third is operational: e.g. clear audit logs and traceability for each request for compliance.
[00:01:35] Priya: OK parity on entity extraction makes sense, we usually do a prompt/eval set. For latency, just to set expectations, if you're on hosted Redwood API with batching there are levers — batching, prefix caching — that usually reduce cost but can add some tail. We can propose a config that targets p95 < 450ms for 1k token-ish prompts.
[00:01:58] Samir: Our typical prompt length is 400-800 tokens, sometimes up to 1.2k. Concurrency per service is around 120 active requests during peak, with spikes to ~200 for short bursts.
[00:02:12] Alex: Good — that's exactly the workload profile we need. We'll capture the concurrency matrix as an action item. Liam, from SRE on SLA, is there a hard requirement for queuing or do you have elasticity you can tolerate?
[00:02:25] Liam: We can tolerate short queueing but prefer soft failover to a cheaper model rather than very long queues. Also, we need deterministic KV cache behavior — we call it KV cache but we sometimes see it transcribed as kv cash — don't worry about that — basically prefix caching for multi-turn.

[00:02:50] Priya: For the POC we'll propose two tracks: Track A is OpenAI-compatible endpoints (so you can point your existing SDK and change minimal code), Track B is direct Redwood SDK integration for more observability and advanced control (batching/concur configs). We can run both in parallel during the pilot.
[00:03:08] Dasha: Running both is interesting. Our product team wants the least dev lift; engineering might prefer SDK for extra hooks.

[00:03:30] Samir: A couple of technical constraints: our auth uses SAML SSO for admin console, and API keys are rotated daily via a token broker. Also all keys must be wrapped with customer KMS if hosted in our VPC.
[00:03:45] Alex: Sounds good — Redwood supports SAML and we've got KMS integrations; we'll include the KMS/HSM notes in the security pack.

[00:04:05] Priya: On the function-calling/ tool-calling side, I want to confirm: you're looking for structured output that must validate against your JSON schema and support partial failures? Example: tool X might fail but model returns fallback structured output with error field.
[00:04:20] Dasha: Exactly. We need deterministic keys: {entityList, confidence, sourceDocId, spans, error} — ideally validated post-generation.
[00:04:30] Priya: We'll include Redwood's structured-output validator in the harness. Note: function-calling semantics and the OpenAI-style function_call parameter are emulated in the OpenAI-compat layer but there are subtle differences — sometimes function names or types get slight tokenization differences, so we'll include a small shim to normalize.

[00:04:55] Samir: Okay that shim is fine as long as it keeps stable field names. Also we use a downstream orchestrator that expects strictly typed fields, so if the JSON is malformed we need a deterministic fallback.

[00:05:20] Alex: Noted. We'll make sure the POC includes a JSON schema and a set of negative tests where model returns malformed output and we exercise the validator/fallback path.

[00:05:40] Priya: Now benchmarks. We propose an initial 2-hour load run that includes: steady-state of 120 concurrent connections at realistic token sizes, 30 minute spike to 200 concurrency, and a set of quality evals against your labelled dataset. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per token, and error rates including structured-output validation failures.
[00:06:02] Liam: For billing / cost visibility — we need per-route token and cost breakdowns, and traceability back to request ids for chargeback. Is that in Redwood Console?
[00:06:12] Alex: Yes Console exposes token-level breakdown and tracing hooks per request id. If you go SDK route you get additional tags surfaced for internal cost allocation.

[00:06:30] Dasha: Timeline wise we want a 4-week POC: week 0 is kickoff and data exchange, week 1 bench harness + openai-compat shim, week 2 run benchmarks and iterate, week 3 pilot-internal traffic with synthetic mix, week 4 review and decision. Is that reasonable?
[00:06:47] Priya: That's realistic. We often compress but 4 weeks gives time for security review and tune. Also we usually suggest a mid-pilot canary route to test private deployment options.

[00:07:05] Samir: A question on model variants — do you have quantized variants that preserve quality? We care about cost.
[00:07:12] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles — for the pilot we can run the same model in float and q4_0 and report delta in throughput/latency/quality. We'll include that in the benchmark matrix.

[00:07:30] Liam: For private deployment feasibility we need network diagrams, firewall rules, and expected peering latency. We'll need an on-prem packaging note for air-gapped later.
[00:07:41] Alex: We'll attach network diagrams and an on-prem checklist. For the initial POC we'll keep data synthetic unless you want to bring a small redacted set.

[00:08:00] Dasha: We'll send redacted samples, but for legal we'll need to see retention policies and audit log retention times.
[00:08:08] Alex: Understood. That goes in the security pack.

[00:08:25] Priya: On the integration pattern — if you use OpenAI-compatible endpoints, your existing call pattern remains: POST /v1/chat/completions (or the embeddings endpoint). We'll support function_call and our shim will convert to Redwood runtime call. SDK integration gives you streaming and per-token logging hooks and easier structured output enforcement.
[00:08:45] Samir: Quick follow-up: does the OpenAI-compat path support streaming partial JSON so our orchestrator can start work before full response?
[00:08:54] Priya: Yes, we support streaming, but note that partial JSON streaming requires a small client-side parser; we typically stream chunked tokens and the SDK can reassemble safely. There are edge cases where tokenization can split multibyte sequences and break naive parsers. We'll share our streaming parsing guidance.

[00:09:20] Dasha: Regarding acceptance criteria for structured output — we want 95% pass on schema validation for the golden prompt set, otherwise it's not acceptable.
[00:09:29] Priya: We'll add that gate. Also define what counts as 'pass' — exact matching keys plus value types, or tolerant matching?
[00:09:36] Dasha: Exact keys and types for fields we use in downstream. For free-text fields we allow fuzzier scoring.

[00:09:50] Alex: Ok making note — acceptance: >=95% strict schema pass on golden set; p95 latency < 450ms on production-like tokens; sustain 120 concurrency with spike handling; security artifacts provided.

[00:10:12] Samir: Another operational note — we do daily key rotation via a token broker, so short-lived API keys for test are fine but anything long-lived needs KMS wrap.
[00:10:22] Alex: Good to know — we'll make test keys ephemeral and document KMS instructions.

[00:10:40] Priya: On the benchmark harness details — we'll provide a dockerized runner that can be dropped into your CI or run from Redwood infra. It will exercise both the OpenAI-compat and SDK endpoints, run quality evals, and output CSV/JSON results including the structured-output validation stats.
[00:11:00] Liam: We want artifact reproducibility; can we get the harness config in code as a repo?
[00:11:06] Priya: Yes we'll push a GitHub repo and invite you.

[00:11:25] Samir: For the golden prompt set we have about 1.2k labelled examples. We can provide 200 for the pilot as a stratified sample.
[00:11:34] Dasha: We'll include edge cases too — multilingual, nested entities.

[00:11:45] Priya: Great. For metrics we'll report: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost/token estimate, schema-pass rate, hallucination rate (we'll run a simple heuristic), and failure modes where the model returns non-json.

[00:12:05] Alex: I want to surface one caveat — OpenAI-compat endpoints give a convenience lift but if you need deep per-request routing (region/capacity tier/fallback to smaller model) the SDK gives more control for that. We often recommend starting with compat then migrating hot paths to SDK if you need advanced routing.
[00:12:27] Samir: That's reasonable. For minimal change we'll start compat for the non-critical path, SDK for critical routes.

[00:12:40] Dasha: Any hard blockers we should be aware of? Security aside, are there any known issues around function calling in compat mode?
[00:12:48] Priya: Mostly edge cases in name normalization and certain rare tokenization differences that can change the function signature string. Our shim handles that but we'll include negative tests.

[00:13:05] Liam: Instrumentation — we need a request id per request and the ability to pull traces for correlation with our logs.
[00:13:13] Alex: Redwood Console exposes request id tracing and you can also pass your own client_request_id; we'll ensure the harness demos that.

[00:13:30] Samir: On cost visibility, will the POC show comparative numbers vs OpenAI that we currently use?
[00:13:38] Priya: We'll run a comparative analysis if you can provide recent invoices or representative usage. Otherwise we'll do unit-cost extrapolation based on tokens and model.

[00:13:55] Dasha: For the pilot decision criteria: 1) meets acceptance gates, 2) operational fit (security/peering), 3) cost math within 20% of current runbook, and 4) migration effort under 2 sprint-equivalents.

[00:14:12] Alex: Nice crisp decision criteria — we'll digest that and reflect in the summary.

[00:14:25] Priya: Anything else on tooling? We mentioned structured-output validator; we also have an eval harness that does regression alerts if quality drops vs baseline prompts. That's optional but useful for longer pilots.
[00:14:39] Dasha: Please include that as an opt-in during the pilot.

[00:14:50] Samir: Do you support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller cheaper model if latency spikes?
[00:14:57] Priya: Yes Redwood has routing policies and automatic fallbacks by capacity tier, we can set rules to spill to a cheaper model in high load but the quality delta will be measured.

[00:15:15] Alex: Let's capture concrete dates: we'll exchange artifacts this week, Redwood to produce benchmark harness by 2026-12-09, initial run week of 2026-12-13, mid-pilot checkpoint 2026-12-17, final review 2027-01-07. Any conflicts?
[00:15:32] Dasha: Those look OK, holiday windows noted for late December — maybe pause for 10 days if necessary but keep final review early January.

[00:15:50] Priya: For the POC we suggest this runbook: Kickoff + security sign-off (week 0), harness iterate (week 1), bench runs & quantify (week 2), internal synthetic traffic (week 3), review & decision (week 4).

[00:16:10] Samir: One small ask — can you include a sample CURL call for the OpenAI-compat endpoint showing function_call and structured output in the quickstart?
[00:16:18] Alex: Absolutely — we'll include that in the repo and the quickstart.

[00:16:35] Dasha: Last question on legal/procurement — for pilot do you require PO? We prefer an MSA in place but pilot can often be started on a trial agreement.
[00:16:44] Alex: Pilot can start under a trial agreement; enterprise contracts and PO typically come after successful pilot. We'll route through our legal team for a short trial SOW.

[00:16:55] Liam: Ok thanks. We'll need the security pack early as some internal teams need to review for any hosted endpoints.

[00:17:10] Alex: Noted. We'll push the security pack by 2026-12-06.

[00:17:25] Priya: Any other technical clarifications?
[00:17:28] Samir: Two quick ones: 1) Do you support model pinning per route? 2) How do you handle KV cache across turns in the compat shim?
[00:17:36] Priya: 1) Yes model pinning per route is supported. 2) The compat shim can pass through a session id and Redwood runtime will maintain KV cache keyed by session — we expose TTL and explicit invalidation hooks. Small note: in compat mode we may expose those via headers, SDK has more first class apis.

[00:18:00] Dasha: Great. I think that's most of it. Can we recap next steps?
[00:18:05] Alex: Sure. Recap: Redwood to share security docs + quickstart + CURL examples (Alex) by 2026-12-06; Priya to deliver benchmark harness and push repo by 2026-12-09; Nimbus to share 200-sample golden prompts and 7d traces (Samir) by 2026-12-07; initial benchmark run week of 2026-12-13; mid pilot checkpoint 2026-12-17; final review 2027-01-07.
[00:18:33] Dasha: Confirmed. We'll also schedule the calendar invite for the mid-pilot check.

[00:18:45] Liam: Thanks everyone.
[00:18:50] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with an email and the repo invite.
[00:18:55] Priya: Thanks, bye.

[00:19:00] (END)
